scope.scopeNotesMd: The R6 package does not contain `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductPharmaceutical.json`. The R6 package index instead contains the R6 regulatory product family (`AdministrableProductDefinition`, `MedicinalProductDefinition`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, `Ingredient`, `PackagedProductDefinition`, `RegulatedAuthorization`, and `ClinicalUseDefinition`), and `CodeSystem/fhir-old-types` lists `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` as an old resource name no longer used. narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProductPharmaceutical R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` is not present as an R6 resource. R4 instances using `resourceType: MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` are therefore hard invalid in R6 without migration. The closest R6 model is not a pure rename: it is a split, centered on `AdministrableProductDefinition` and linked to `MedicinalProductDefinition`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, `Ingredient`, and packaging resources.

## Scope
I compared the R4 StructureDefinition with the absent assigned R6 path, the R6 package index, the R6 old-type code system, and the likely successor resources. Inherited base-resource and datatype changes are deliberately excluded from `findings[]`.

## Main migration themes
The main migration work is identity replacement, creation of required lifecycle `status`, and deciding where composition, manufactured-item, device, and product-level links belong in the R6 split model. Straight path-copying is unsafe because several R4 elements either changed representation (`ingredient`, `characteristics`) or gained successor-only constraints (`apd-1`).

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the removal of the resource identity. The next highest risks are the required R6 `AdministrableProductDefinition.status`, the ingredient reference-to-code/resource split, and narrowing of `device` from `0..*` to `0..1` with integral-device semantics.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for successor selection and data-preserving transforms, especially where R4 instances rely on `MedicinalProductIngredient` references, arbitrary characteristic status codes, multiple devices, or product routes recorded both on a medicinal product and its administrable form.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could have been made less disruptive by retaining a deprecated R6 resource alias or by keeping old element representations alongside the new model for one release. The split model is probably justified by improved regulatory modeling, but it is not wire-compatible.

## Follow-up analysis
Run separate artifact reports for `AdministrableProductDefinition`, `Ingredient`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, `MedicinalProductDefinition`, and `PackagedProductDefinition`, and review any official cross-version maps when available.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` is removed from the R6 resource set, so R4 instances are not directly valid R6. The top migration concerns are resource identity replacement, required R6 lifecycle status, ingredient/device representation changes, and successor-only route/product constraints. The main uncertainty is the exact official migration intent because no computable cross-version map was available locally.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should not attempt a simple `resourceType` rename. A safe migration needs to construct an `AdministrableProductDefinition`, assign a publication `status`, map dose form and route content, decide whether ingredients remain simple codes or become `Ingredient` resources, move manufactured item context to `ManufacturedItemDefinition`/`producedFrom`, and move co-packaged devices to packaging/product-level structures where appropriate. R6-to-R4 conversion is also lossy because R6 has optional dose form and new product/manufacturing links that R4 `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` cannot carry directly.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the R4 resource is absent in R6 and treated as an old type. Confidence is medium for detailed element-by-element migration recommendations because they infer successor mapping from local R6 StructureDefinitions rather than an official R4-to-R6 ConceptMap or narrative migration guide. Terminology impact is limited by absent expansions, but most R6 bindings on retained coded fields are example-strength and therefore not direct validation breaks.

findings.title: MedicinalProductPharmaceutical has no R6 StructureDefinition and is treated as an old resource type

oldState.summary: R4 defines a concrete DomainResource specialization named MedicinalProductPharmaceutical.

semanticText.short: A pharmaceutical product described in terms of its composition and dose form
semanticText.definition: A pharmaceutical product described in terms of its composition and dose form.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` is a concrete resource type with its own canonical StructureDefinition and JSON/XML resource identity.

newState.summary: R6 has no MedicinalProductPharmaceutical StructureDefinition; the closest local successor is AdministrableProductDefinition, with adjacent split resources.

semanticText.short: A medicinal product in the final form, suitable for administration - after any mixing of multiple components
semanticText.definition: A medicinal product in the final form which is suitable for administering to a patient after any mixing of multiple components, dissolution etc. has been performed.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 does not define the old resource type. The R6 `fhir-old-types` CodeSystem lists `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical`, and the package instead provides `AdministrableProductDefinition` plus related regulatory product resources.

facts.note: The assigned R6 path is absent.
The old resource name is not indexed as an R6 StructureDefinition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `AdministrableProductDefinition` contains most local R4 element concepts (`administrableDoseForm`, `unitOfPresentation`, `ingredient`, `device`, `property`/characteristics, and `routeOfAdministration`), but R6 also distributes product, manufactured item, ingredient, and package responsibilities to separate resources.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format and validation break. An R4 JSON instance whose `resourceType` is `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` cannot validate against the R6 core resource set because that StructureDefinition is absent. R6 content in the successor model also cannot be represented as the same R4 resource without choosing a cross-version transform.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Regulatory product catalogs and medicinal product master data that used the R4 resource need explicit migration before exchange or validation against R6.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace the R4 medicinal product resource family with a more explicit R6 regulatory product model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` as the R6 administrable-product resource identity and update its definitions and content there.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of an explicit administrable product definition and richer regulatory product graph is reasonable. However, the R4 resource already modeled the pharmaceutical or administrable product aspect, so changing the root wire identity to `AdministrableProductDefinition` was not clearly required to meet that goal. Field-level remodels may still need separate justification, but the root `resourceType` break itself appears probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept the R4 canonical/resource type `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical`, revised its definition toward administrable product semantics, and added the R6 relationships and elements under that resource. That would preserve old `resourceType` values, REST routes, references, generated classes, and FHIRPath roots. The tradeoff is a less tidy name than `AdministrableProductDefinition`; if both names were normative, duplicate resource identities could persist, so the cleaner compatibility path would be retention rather than a parallel alias.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves resourceType, reference, and endpoint compatibility, but leaves a legacy, less consistent name in the R6 definition-resource family.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` as a concrete resource.
The assigned R6 StructureDefinition file is absent.
R6 lists `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` in the old-types CodeSystem for old resource names no longer used.
evidence.quote: description: An old resource name no longer used in this version of FHIR (deleted or renamed).

examples.examplesMd: The examples are intentionally minimal. The R4 fragment satisfies the local mandatory R4 fields but fails R6 identity because the resource type no longer exists. A real migration must also handle identifiers, ingredients, devices, and product/manufacturing links.

findings.narrativeMd: The assigned resource is removed rather than carried forward as a same-name R6 artifact. This affects validators, parsers, generated model classes, REST endpoints, search compartments, and any code switching on `resourceType`. Even if most element meanings can be mapped to `AdministrableProductDefinition`, the old resource cannot be accepted as-is by an R6 system.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid is guaranteed for any standalone R4 instance because R6 has no corresponding core StructureDefinition. R6-to-R4 is also risky because the successor model can express links and split resources that have no single field in R4 `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit migration layer. Choose whether each R4 instance becomes an `AdministrableProductDefinition` alone or an APD plus `MedicinalProductDefinition`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, `Ingredient`, and packaging resources. Test validators with old `resourceType`, migrated APD, and mixed resource graphs. Do not rely on automatic model-class renaming.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change appears to support a richer regulatory product model, but it is not backward compatible. A deprecated alias or wrapper could have made old wire content acceptable while encouraging migration, but at the cost of maintaining two overlapping resource models.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The identity break is certain; exact successor mapping is inferred from local R6 StructureDefinitions and should be checked against official migration guidance if available.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 defines a concrete `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` resource, while the R6 package has no same-name StructureDefinition and instead carries `AdministrableProductDefinition` plus related product-definition resources. This is a top-level wire/API break: an existing instance, REST type, reference target, generated model class, or switch on `resourceType` cannot be accepted by an R6 system without an explicit transform. FMM 0 means the resource did not carry a strong stability promise, but the break is broad for any adopter and the medicinal-product regulatory domain is implementation-relevant enough that a pure resource identity replacement deserves renewed design attention.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition id/type/url are MedicinalProductPharmaceutical; status draft; local maturity map says FMM 0 and trial-use.
R6 assigned StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductPharmaceutical.json is absent; R6 package index contains AdministrableProductDefinition and adjacent product-definition resources.
R6 CodeSystem/fhir-old-types contains MedicinalProductPharmaceutical as an old type.

FHIR R4 public page marks MedicinalProductPharmaceutical as Trial Use; EMA PMS page says an ISO IDMP-compatible HL7 FHIR data submission format replaces XEVPRM, and the DADI webinar page says new forms align with EU IGs using FHIR.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use substantially softens the stability expectation and prevents assuming broad deployed impact from the break alone. I still weight this as concerning because it is a resource identity/API break and the regulatory product domain has official FHIR/IDMP implementation activity.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 instances with `resourceType: MedicinalProductPharmaceutical`, REST routes, references, generated classes, and FHIRPath roots have no same-name R6 base resource.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base design plausibly existed: keep `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` as the administrable-product resource identity, or provide a deprecated same-wire alias for a transition, while adding the richer R6 links and definitions. The tradeoff is a less tidy resource name and possible duplicate identity if both names remain first-class, but the pure identity break looks more disruptive than necessary.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Critical impact and Yes alternative judgment: the top-level break is real and a less-breaking identity design is plausible, but the existing report overstates expected prevalence given FMM 0 and only indirect production-use evidence.

findings.title: Likely successor requires a new modifier lifecycle status

oldState.summary: R4 MedicinalProductPharmaceutical has no root lifecycle status element.
oldState.narrativeMd: An R4 instance can be locally complete with only `administrableDoseForm` and at least one `routeOfAdministration`; no root `status` is required or available on the R4 resource.

newState.summary: R6 AdministrableProductDefinition.status is mandatory, modifier, summary, and required-bound to publication-status.

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 has no comparable root element. The R6 required ValueSet includes draft, active, retired, and unknown.

flags.isModifierReason: The status contains codes that mark the resource as not currently valid.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 successor cannot be valid without a lifecycle status. Because this status is a modifier, consumers are expected to account for values such as `retired` or `draft` in business logic.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This is a new root element on the likely successor; no R4 `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` root element has equivalent path or cardinality.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A migrated APD missing `status` fails R6 validation. Runtime risk is high because status is a modifier and may affect whether content should be used. R6-to-R4 conversion loses this lifecycle/modifier information unless an extension or companion resource is used.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Using a retired or draft administrable product as if active can have regulatory and catalog-management consequences.

justification.inferredGoal: Make lifecycle state explicit and filterable for administrable product definitions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `status` optional, or give absence an explicit unknown meaning while requiring status through profiles or best-practice rules.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Making lifecycle state explicit is a reasonable R6 goal, especially because `status` is a modifier whose retired value affects whether applications should use the definition. A less-breaking base design exists, but it would materially reduce the guarantee that every administrable product can be filtered by lifecycle state. Given that safety and conformance tradeoff, the required modifier status is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have left `status` at `0..1`, used meaning-when-missing or a default-like interpretation of unknown, and required the field in implementation profiles. That would let R4-derived instances validate without manufacturing a lifecycle state. The alternative is only partial because generic R6 consumers could not rely on status being present, and profile-level requirements would not protect base-level exchange from retired or unknown definitions being processed incorrectly.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances without synthetic status values, but weakens base lifecycle guarantees and safe filtering of retired definitions.

evidence.detail: No R4 root `status` element exists for MedicinalProductPharmaceutical.
R6 APD status is 1..1 code, required-bound to publication-status, isModifier true, and isSummary true.
The required code system concepts are draft, active, retired, and unknown.

examples.examplesMd: The illustrative migration chooses `active`; a real transform needs a policy for deriving or defaulting status, and defaulting may be clinically or regulatorily unsafe.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 APD adds a mandatory lifecycle status that R4 MPP did not have. This is not just an optional metadata enrichment: validators reject missing status, and generated R6 classes may require it. Because it is a modifier, downstream systems also need to understand how draft, retired, active, and unknown content should be used.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance can be valid with no status. The corresponding R6 APD is invalid unless a required status code is supplied. R6-to-R4 conversion cannot store the status in a native R4 MPP field, so the information is either lost or must be carried by extension or a parallel migration artifact.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a deterministic status policy before migration. If status is unknown, use the R6 `unknown` code rather than inventing a local code. Tests should cover omitted status, each allowed publication-status value, and business rules that must suppress retired or draft products.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Requiring status in the base resource improves uniformity but is breaking for old data. A profile-level requirement would have preserved R4-compatible data but would not guarantee lifecycle state for all base R6 instances.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding assumes `AdministrableProductDefinition` is the migration target for the assigned R4 resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The likely R6 successor requires `AdministrableProductDefinition.status` as a 1..1 required-bound modifier, while R4 `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` has no native lifecycle status. A forward migration must supply a status value and business logic must treat draft/retired/unknown appropriately. That is real migration work, but lifecycle state is a reasonable base requirement for a regulatory definition resource, and making it optional would weaken generic R6 filtering and safe use.
keyEvidence: R4 differential has no MedicinalProductPharmaceutical.status element.
R6 AdministrableProductDefinition.status is 1..1 code, required-bound to publication-status, isModifier true, and isSummary true.
The R6 status comment says it allows filtering of administrable products appropriate for use.
EMA PMS/DADI pages support regulatory FHIR/IDMP relevance, though not direct proof of broad R4 MPP production use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers the compatibility burden, but lifecycle status is central to regulatory product use and the R6 successor is FMM 2, so I do not dismiss the migration burden as mere metadata churn.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid on the successor plus runtime/API/codegen: a migrated APD without `status` fails R6 validation, and modifier-aware consumers must account for non-active states; R6-to-R4 loses the status unless carried outside native R4 MPP.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could make `status` 0..1, define absence as unknown, or require it only in profiles. That would preserve more transformed R4 data but would prevent base R6 consumers from relying on lifecycle state, especially for retired or draft definitions.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment: the break is genuine, but the stricter base requirement appears proportionate.

findings.title: Ingredient changed from references to a split code-or-Ingredient model

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 stores ingredient links as references to separate `MedicinalProductIngredient` resources.

newState.summary: R6 APD ingredient is 0..* CodeableConcept for simple coded ingredients; detailed ingredients are represented by incoming Ingredient resources or manufactured-item links.

binding.description: This value set includes all substance codes from SNOMED CT - provided as an exemplar value set.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 APD inline ingredient binding is example-strength; the primary breaking issue is representation, not required terminology.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 APD supports a basic coded ingredient inline, but detailed composition belongs to `Ingredient` resources with `Ingredient.for` pointing to APD/MPD/MID or to manufactured item relationships.

facts.note: The detailed R6 target is an incoming `Ingredient` resource rather than the inline APD field type.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element name remains `ingredient` on the closest successor, but its type and modeling pattern changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 MPP instance that carries `ingredient` as a Reference cannot be copied into the APD `ingredient` field, which expects CodeableConcept. Preserving detailed ingredient semantics requires creating R6 `Ingredient` resources and satisfying their required fields. Conversely, an R6 APD with only a coded ingredient does not provide an R4 `Reference(MedicinalProductIngredient)` without synthesizing a target resource.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ingredient identity and strength are clinically and regulatorily important; lossy transforms can misstate product composition.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow simple coded ingredient lists while moving detailed ingredient composition to the standalone R6 Ingredient resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a reference-valued ingredient path, or add a code-or-reference choice while introducing detailed `Ingredient` resources.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of supporting both simple coded ingredients and detailed standalone ingredient definitions is reasonable. Replacing the old direct reference with a coded ingredient list is a hard shape and graph break, but a fully compatible alternative would have to carry old direct references beside incoming `Ingredient.for` links and coded summaries. Those duplicate-representation and target-resource tradeoffs make the break probably justified rather than fully avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `ingredient` as a reference, retargeted it to `Ingredient` or accepted a deprecated `MedicinalProductIngredient` target, and added a separate coded ingredient element or choice. That would preserve many R4 payloads with direct ingredient references. It is partial because the old target resource is also absent in R6, and supporting direct APD ingredient references, incoming `Ingredient.for` links, and coded summaries would require precedence and consistency rules for overlapping ingredient facts.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves referenced ingredients for common migrations, but leaves competing ingredient channels and depends on retaining or mapping the old target resource.

evidence.detail: R4 ingredient is a repeating Reference to MedicinalProductIngredient.
R6 APD ingredient is a repeating CodeableConcept with example substance-codes binding.
R6 detailed ingredients are standalone resources that can point to APD, MPD, or MID and have mandatory status, role, and substance.

examples.examplesMd: The `Ingredient` example is illustrative and not a complete strength-preserving transform. A real transform must inspect the referenced R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient`.

findings.narrativeMd: The ingredient element keeps a similar name but no longer carries the same kind of value. R4 references a detailed ingredient resource. R6 APD can carry only simple coded ingredients inline; detailed ingredients are separate incoming `Ingredient` resources. This is a common source of migration bugs because code generated for `ingredient: Reference[]` cannot be reused for `ingredient: CodeableConcept[]`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 fragment with `ingredient.reference` is not valid as an APD inline ingredient. Preserving content usually requires dereferencing the old `MedicinalProductIngredient`, creating one or more R6 `Ingredient` resources, and linking them back with `Ingredient.for`. R6 APD coded ingredients are not cleanly representable in R4 MPP without manufacturing a referenced R4 ingredient resource.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify each R4 ingredient reference as simple coded content or detailed composition. For simple cases, map to APD `ingredient` CodeableConcept. For detailed cases, create R6 `Ingredient` resources and carry role, substance, strength, manufacturer, and allergen information there. Test both inline-code and detailed-reference cases, including missing required R6 `Ingredient.status`, `role`, and `substance`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 design likely improves modeling by separating simple codes from rich ingredients, but replacing a reference with a code is not backward compatible. A transitional choice type would have reduced conversion friction but introduced duplicate ways to say the same thing.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Full safety assessment depends on separate analysis of R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` versus R6 `Ingredient`.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `ingredient` is a repeating reference to `MedicinalProductIngredient`; R6 APD `ingredient` is a repeating `CodeableConcept`, with detailed ingredients represented through separate `Ingredient` resources that point back to the product graph. That changes both the JSON shape and the graph model, so direct copying is invalid and preserving detailed ingredient information may require dereferencing the old resource and constructing new R6 resources. The path is important, but the R6 design has a coherent goal: distinguish simple coded ingredient summaries from full ingredient definitions.
keyEvidence: R4 MedicinalProductPharmaceutical.ingredient is 0..* Reference(MedicinalProductIngredient).
R6 AdministrableProductDefinition.ingredient is 0..* CodeableConcept with example substance-codes binding.
R6 Ingredient.for targets MedicinalProductDefinition, AdministrableProductDefinition, and ManufacturedItemDefinition; Ingredient.status, role, and substance are mandatory.
EMA PMS page documents ISO IDMP-compatible HL7 FHIR product-data submission, supporting domain relevance but not exact R4 MPP deployment prevalence.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the stability expectation, but ingredient composition is core regulatory and safety-significant product data, so lossy or expert-dependent mapping still matters.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and R6-to-R4 loss: an R4 `ingredient.reference` cannot populate APD `ingredient` directly, while an R6 coded ingredient or incoming `Ingredient` graph may not round-trip to an R4 reference without creating synthetic target resources.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could have used a code-or-reference shape or kept a reference-valued path retargeted to `Ingredient`. That would ease common R4 migrations, but it would introduce overlapping ingredient channels beside `Ingredient.for`, create precedence/consistency rules, and still need a story for the removed R4 target resource.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment: the migration burden is substantial, but the base design tradeoffs make the break probably acceptable.

findings.title: Device cardinality narrows and semantics change to an integral device

oldState.summary: R4 device is 0..* Reference(DeviceDefinition) for accompanying devices.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can list multiple accompanying device references directly on the pharmaceutical resource.

newState.summary: R6 APD device is 0..1 Reference(DeviceDefinition) and is described as an integral device, not co-packaged devices.

semanticText.short: A device that is integral to the medicinal product, in effect being considered as an ingredient of the medicinal product
semanticText.definition: A device that is integral to the medicinal product, in effect being considered as an ingredient of the medicinal product. This is not intended for devices that are just co-packaged.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same target resource type but allows only one APD device and narrows the intended meaning to integral devices.

facts.newValue: Integral device; not intended for devices that are just co-packaged.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements are named `device` and reference `DeviceDefinition`, but the R6 cardinality and long definition are narrower.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with zero or one integral device can migrate directly. R4 instances with multiple devices, or devices that are merely accompanying/co-packaged, need restructuring and can fail R6 validation or conformance review if copied into APD.device.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misclassifying a co-packaged device as integral may alter product definition and regulatory interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate integral devices from co-packaged devices and product-package contents.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `device` repeatable and qualify integral versus co-packaged devices, or retain legacy `device` while adding a distinct integral-device path.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating integral devices from merely co-packaged devices is a reasonable R6 modeling goal. A less-breaking design could preserve repeatability and add role semantics, but old R4 instances do not reliably state which accompanying devices are integral, and retaining a broad legacy field would compete with package-level modeling. Because the alternative preserves only part of the old meaning and has material consistency costs, the narrowing is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base alternative would retain `device` as `0..*` and qualify each reference as integral or co-packaged, or leave the old broad `device` field during transition while adding a new integral-device element. This would reduce validation failures for R4 instances with multiple devices. The cost is that migration still needs human or source-system classification, and devices could be represented both on `AdministrableProductDefinition` and in package contents with conflicting roles.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves more old device arrays, but requires classification absent from R4 and risks duplicate APD/package device relationships.

evidence.detail: R4 device is 0..* Reference(DeviceDefinition), definition `Accompanying device.`
R6 APD device is 0..1 Reference(DeviceDefinition) and not intended for devices that are just co-packaged.
R6 packaging can represent contained devices among package contents.

examples.examplesMd: If both R4 devices are integral, a single APD cannot carry them both in `device`; if one is co-packaged, it should not be copied to APD.device.

findings.narrativeMd: The device element looks deceptively similar because it still references `DeviceDefinition`, but its capacity and meaning changed. R4 allowed a list of accompanying devices. R6 APD allows a single device and says it is integral to the medicinal product, not merely co-packaged.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with more than one device become invalid if mapped directly to APD.device because R6 max is `1`. R4 co-packaged devices may remain syntactically valid if a single value is copied, but semantically wrong. R6-to-R4 is easier because an APD single device can fit in R4's repeating field, though it may lose the integral-device nuance.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inspect every R4 device. Keep at most one integral device on APD.device. Move co-packaged devices to `PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.containedItem.item` or product-level structures according to the broader product migration. Tests should include zero, one, multiple, integral, and co-packaged device scenarios.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Narrowing the base field was probably intended to clarify product modeling. A role-coded repeating element would have been less breaking but would not force a clean distinction between integral and packaged devices.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Migration choices depend on package context that may be outside the old R4 MPP instance.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R4 element allowed multiple accompanying `DeviceDefinition` references. The R6 APD element allows at most one `DeviceDefinition` and narrows the meaning to a device integral to the product, not a merely co-packaged item. R4 data with several devices, or with package devices rather than integral devices, needs classification and possibly relocation to packaging structures. That is a real migration issue, but it reflects a reasonable model cleanup rather than an arbitrary constraint.
keyEvidence: R4 MedicinalProductPharmaceutical.device is 0..* Reference(DeviceDefinition) with definition `Accompanying device.`
R6 AdministrableProductDefinition.device is 0..1 Reference(DeviceDefinition) and is defined as an integral device, not co-packaged.
R6 PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.containedItem.item can reference DeviceDefinition for package contents.
No quick evidence found that this specific low-FMM path is widely used in production.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the concern, and the path appears narrower than the resource identity or ingredient changes. The regulatory interpretation of integral versus co-packaged devices still keeps it above a no-problem category.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid for R4 arrays with more than one device, plus semantic/conformance risk when a single R4 accompanying device is actually co-packaged rather than integral.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept `device` repeatable with a role or added a separate integral-device path while retaining the old broad field. That would preserve more R4 arrays, but old data often lacks the integral/co-packaged distinction and duplicate representation with packaging contents would need reconciliation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment: the break is real, but FMM 0 and likely narrower prevalence make the practical impact less certain than High suggests.

findings.title: Characteristics are remodeled as properties with a value[x] and required-bound status

oldState.summary: R4 characteristics has required `code` and optional unconstrained CodeableConcept `status`.

semanticText.short: Characteristics e.g. a products onset of action
semanticText.definition: Characteristics e.g. a products onset of action.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 models a characteristic primarily as a required `code`, with optional `status`; there is no separate value element.

newState.summary: R6 APD property has required `type`, optional polymorphic `value[x]`, and optional `status` required-bound to publication-status.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 did not bind characteristic status. The R4 short text mentioned assigned or pending; those are not publication-status codes unless represented by a local coding outside required binding rules.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates characteristic type from characteristic value and constrains `property.status` to publication-status when present.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `property` definition and short text match the R4 `characteristics` concept, but the internal child model changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 characteristic codes can usually map to R6 property.type, but old code paths and generated classes break because the element and child names changed. R4 characteristic.status values that are not publication-status codes fail if mapped to R6 property.status. R6 property.value[x] has no native R4 MPP location, making reverse conversion lossy.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Most risks are data loss or catalog semantics rather than direct clinical safety, but product characteristics can influence dispensing and regulatory review.

justification.inferredGoal: Model characteristics as typed properties with explicit values and lifecycle status.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `characteristics` and `characteristics.code`, adding optional `value[x]` and `status` refinements instead of renaming the backbone to `property`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of turning characteristics into typed properties with values and optional lifecycle status is reasonable. The supplied definitions do not show that this required changing the wire path from `characteristics.code` to `property.type`; the same data model could have been expressed by retaining the R4 backbone name and adding optional children. Because that alternative has modest long-term cost and avoids a path break, this rename/remodel was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would use `characteristics.code` as the property type and add optional `characteristics.value[x]` plus optional `characteristics.status` with the R6 publication-status binding. Existing R4 instances containing only coded characteristics would remain valid, while R6 could still carry richer property values. The main tradeoff is living with the less generic `characteristics`/`code` names; adding both `characteristics` and `property` would create duplicate same-resource representations, but simply retaining the old names avoids that duplication.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Leaves older terminology in the base resource, but avoids duplicate representations and preserves existing characteristic arrays.

evidence.detail: R4 characteristic has required code and optional status with no binding.
R6 property has required type, optional polymorphic value, and status required-bound to publication-status.

examples.examplesMd: The status mapping from local `pending` to publication-status `draft` is illustrative and requires domain agreement.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 `characteristics` becomes R6 APD `property`. The obvious mapping is `characteristics.code` to `property.type`, but R6 adds `property.value[x]` and constrains status when present. This affects generated models, FHIRPath expressions, and any downstream code that assumed a characteristic was fully expressed by its code.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A direct path copy is invalid because R6 does not have `characteristics.code`; it has `property.type`. If R4 status uses local assigned/pending codes, mapping to R6 `property.status` can violate the required publication-status binding. Conversely, R6 property values such as `valueQuantity` cannot be represented in R4 MPP without extensions or loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 `characteristics` repeat to R6 `property`. Move `code` to `type`; map status only through an agreed terminology policy; preserve unmappable status or values with extensions if needed. Add tests for characteristics without status, with local status codes, and with R6 value[x] reverse conversion.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The property/value design is semantically stronger but could have been introduced with a deprecated alias or choice. The binding change on status is the least backward-compatible part and may require manual terminology mapping.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 status binding appears stricter than the R4 short text examples, so terminology review is recommended.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `characteristics.code` maps naturally to R6 `property.type`, and R6 adds useful value and status structure. The concerning part is the avoidable wire-path change from `characteristics`/`code` to `property`/`type`, plus a stricter required binding on `property.status` when present. Existing instances that only have a coded characteristic could have remained valid if R6 kept the old names and added optional value/status refinements. Because the likely alternative is modest and preserves the R6 goal, this path deserves another look despite the low maturity.
keyEvidence: R4 MedicinalProductPharmaceutical.characteristics is 0..* with required characteristics.code and optional unbound CodeableConcept status.
R6 AdministrableProductDefinition.property is 0..* with required property.type, optional value[x], and property.status required-bound to publication-status.
R4 status short text mentions assigned or pending; R6 publication-status codes are draft, active, retired, and unknown.
No quick evidence found that this optional low-FMM path is broadly deployed, but it can affect product-catalog semantics where used.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use reduces the stability pressure and keeps this from being high-severity by itself. I still select Revisit because the path rename appears avoidable with a low-cost base design, not because broad production use is proven.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen and potential old-valid/new-invalid: generated clients and FHIRPath expressions using `characteristics.code` break, local status codes may fail if mapped to required-bound `property.status`, and R6 value[x] creates R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could keep `characteristics` and `characteristics.code` as the property type, then add optional `characteristics.value[x]` and a constrained status. That preserves most R4 characteristic arrays and still enables richer R6 properties; the main tradeoff is retaining less generic legacy names.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Yes alternative judgment: I agree a less-breaking design looks plausible, while FMM 0 keeps the practical impact from being treated as broadly high.

findings.title: Administrable dose form is optional in the R6 successor, creating R6-to-R4 representability risk

semanticText.short: The administrable dose form, after necessary reconstitution
semanticText.definition: The administrable dose form, after necessary reconstitution.

oldState.narrativeMd: An R4 MPP is invalid without an administrable dose form.

newState.summary: R6 APD administrableDoseForm is optional 0..1 CodeableConcept with example administrable-dose-form binding.

binding.description: Dose form for a medication, in the form suitable for administering to the patient, after mixing, where necessary.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 binding is example-strength and does not by itself reject non-member codes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 APD allows the dose form to be omitted, even though it remains the closest corresponding element.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element path suffix, type, and definition clearly match.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The decreased minimum is not an R4-to-R6 validation break. It is a reverse-conversion break: an R6 APD can be valid with no dose form, but an R4 MPP cannot.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Missing dose form can reduce clinical or catalog clarity, but the risk depends on use case and whether another R6 resource supplies equivalent information.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow administrable product definitions when dose form is not known or is represented elsewhere.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; decreasing `administrableDoseForm` from mandatory to optional preserves R4 instances in the R4-to-R6 direction.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing administrable product definitions when dose form is unknown or represented elsewhere is a plausible R6 flexibility goal. The cardinality relaxation does not make R4-valid instances invalid after forward migration, so the backward-compatible-alternative question does not apply in the same way as it would for a removal, rename, or stronger constraint.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 validity because R4 instances that contain `administrableDoseForm` still fit the relaxed R6 cardinality. Keeping the element mandatory would improve R6-to-R4 round trips and can be required by compatibility profiles, but that would be a stricter R6 policy rather than an alternative needed to preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 conversion may need a profile requirement, rejection rule, or extension policy for R6 records missing dose form, but that is a downgrade concern.

evidence.detail: R4 min is 1 and max is 1.
R6 APD min is 0 and max is 1.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example omits `administrableDoseForm`; converting it to a valid R4 MPP requires deriving or inventing a dose form.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a loosening for forward migration but a real round-trip problem. An R6 APD can omit a value that R4 requires. Systems that maintain bidirectional R4/R6 compatibility must not assume every R6 APD can become a valid R4 MPP.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is safe for this element because all valid R4 instances have a dose form that R6 can carry. R6-to-R4 is not safe when the dose form is absent; a converter must either derive a value, reject the conversion, or create an invalid/incomplete R4 instance.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For reverse conversion, define a policy for missing dose form: derive from `MedicinalProductDefinition.combinedPharmaceuticalDoseForm`, `ManufacturedItemDefinition.manufacturedDoseForm`, local terminology, or reject conversion. Do not silently populate a placeholder unless a business rule authorizes it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The cardinality decrease is backward compatible for old data but not for round trips. If R6 needed flexibility, a profile could require dose form for systems that need R4 compatibility.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is a forward-compatible relaxation. R4 requires `administrableDoseForm`, and the R6 successor still has the same element and type but lowers the minimum to 0. Any valid R4 instance has a dose form that can be carried into R6. The only issue is reverse conversion from an R6 APD that omits the value, which is important for bidirectional converters but not a base R4-to-R6 break.
keyEvidence: R4 MedicinalProductPharmaceutical.administrableDoseForm is 1..1 CodeableConcept.
R6 AdministrableProductDefinition.administrableDoseForm is 0..1 CodeableConcept with an example binding.
The path suffix and datatype are preserved.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use further softens the concern because the change does not invalidate old instances; it only affects R6-to-R4 downgrade policy.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss only: an R6 APD can omit a dose form that R4 requires, but R4-valid data remains acceptable in the R6 successor shape.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for forward compatibility. Systems that require R4 round-tripping can profile R6 to require the element or reject R6 records that omit it.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium impact framing: the reverse-conversion caveat is real, but for this R4-to-R6 path-level review it is a No problem finding.

findings.title: R6 successor adds product, manufactured-item, code, and description content not native to R4 MPP

oldState.summary: R4 MedicinalProductPharmaceutical has no native formOf, producedFrom, product code, or description fields.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 MPP contains identifiers, dose form, unit, ingredient references, device references, characteristics, and route details, but no explicit link to a parent medicinal product or manufactured item.

newState.summary: R6 APD adds optional formOf Reference(MedicinalProductDefinition), producedFrom Reference(ManufacturedItemDefinition), code Coding, and description markdown.
newState.narrativeMd: These optional R6 fields express graph relationships and product codes that cannot be placed directly in R4 MPP without extensions or related R4 resources.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are local APD elements with no same-name R4 MPP counterpart.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not invalidate R4 data migrating forward. They do create lossy reverse conversion and runtime risk for code that assumes the administrable product has no explicit product/manufactured-item graph context.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing product/manufactured item linkage can affect product identity, preparation, and package/manufacturing interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Connect the administrable product to the broader R6 regulatory product graph.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional R6 `formOf`, `producedFrom`, `code`, and `description` additions do not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Connecting the administrable product to the broader R6 product graph is a reasonable design goal, and the listed fields are optional additions. They increase R6 expressiveness and R6-to-R4 representability risk, but they are not an avoidable R4-to-R6 breaking base-design change.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The backward-compatible-alternative label is not applicable because preserving R4-valid instances does not require a different R6 base design for these optional fields. Extensions on R4 or sidecar resources can help downgrade or round-trip R6 content, but those are conversion/backport mitigations, not evidence that the R6 base should have omitted first-class optional links.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: First-class R6 graph content creates R6-to-R4 loss unless extensions or sidecars are used, but those are downgrade mitigations rather than base-design alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 APD defines optional product links, manufactured-item links, formal product codes, and markdown description.
No corresponding R4 MPP elements exist.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 graph context can sometimes be mapped to other R4 resources, but not to native fields on the scoped R4 MPP alone.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 APD is part of a richer product graph. Fields such as `formOf` and `producedFrom` capture relationships that the R4 MPP resource itself did not hold. This is valuable for R6 but creates loss when reducing the model back to the single R4 artifact.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is not broken by these optional additions. R6-to-R4 is lossy unless the converter emits extensions or coordinates with other R4 medicinal product resources. Generated clients must also account for APD references to resources that were not part of the old local MPP shape.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When migrating forward, populate these links where the source system can identify the parent medicinal product or manufactured item. When converting backward, either preserve them in extensions, map them to other R4 resources outside this report's scope, or document the loss.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additions are reasonable for a split model and are optional, so they are not avoidable breaking changes in the forward direction. They do, however, make round-trip compatibility dependent on broader graph migration.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding is scoped to native R4 MPP fields; a whole-product R4 bundle may have places to carry some relationships outside this artifact.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The listed R6 fields (`formOf`, `producedFrom`, `code`, and `description`) are optional additions on the successor resource. They improve the R6 product graph and do not make any R4 `MedicinalProductPharmaceutical` instance invalid during forward migration. They can be lost when downgrading a richer R6 graph to the single R4 resource, but that is a representability and converter-scope issue, not a breaking base design for old data.
keyEvidence: R6 AdministrableProductDefinition.formOf is 0..* Reference(MedicinalProductDefinition).
R6 producedFrom is 0..* Reference(ManufacturedItemDefinition), code is 0..* Coding, and description is 0..1 markdown.
R4 MedicinalProductPharmaceutical has no native fields with these names, but all listed R6 fields are optional.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use reinforces the No problem judgment because the change is additive for forward compatibility and any loss is in richer R6-to-R4 conversion.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: richer APD graph links and descriptive/code content cannot be stored natively in the scoped R4 resource, but old R4 data is not rejected by these optional additions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable as a less-breaking base R6 alternative. Omitting these optional links would reduce R6 expressiveness rather than preserve additional R4-valid instances; downgrade preservation belongs in profiles, extensions, or broader graph mappings.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium impact emphasis: I agree there is downgrade loss, but optional forward additions are not a material R4-to-R6 compatibility problem.

findings.title: R6 successor adds a cross-resource constraint forbidding duplicate route on formOf product

oldState.summary: R4 MPP has no local invariant coordinating route with a referenced parent product.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 resource requires `routeOfAdministration` but does not have `formOf` and therefore has no comparable cross-resource route constraint.

newState.summary: R6 APD adds invariant apd-1: formOf referenced products must not already have MedicinalProductDefinition.route.

constraints.human: RouteOfAdministration cannot be used when the 'formOf' product already uses MedicinalProductDefinition.route (and vice versa)

newState.narrativeMd: The APD route tree is still mandatory, but APD also says it cannot be used when the referenced `formOf` product already records a route.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The constraint is local to the R6 APD root and has no R4 MPP counterpart because R4 MPP does not link to a parent product.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A migration that creates APD.formOf links to MedicinalProductDefinition resources and also populates routes on both resources can fail R6 validation. The issue is cross-resource and may not be caught by field-level transforms.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Duplicate or conflicting route representation can affect permitted route interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Prevent duplicate route representation on both the administrable product and the parent medicinal product.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Demote `apd-1` to a warning, or make it an error only when APD and parent product routes are demonstrably inconsistent.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Preventing route of administration from being represented authoritatively on both an administrable product and its parent product is a reasonable R6 consistency goal. The error-level invariant can break migrated graphs depending on product-link context, but softer validation would permit duplicate route channels that generic consumers must reconcile. With those material interoperability tradeoffs, the constraint is probably justified with only a partial alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have made `apd-1` a warning or best-practice invariant, or allowed duplication when the APD route and resolved product route are equivalent. That would preserve more R4-derived data where route was copied during graph migration. It is only partial because equivalence across `CodeableConcept` codings can be hard to prove, and allowing duplicate route locations makes it unclear which value is authoritative when they diverge.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves some migrated graphs, but weakens duplicate-route prevention and requires difficult route equivalence or reconciliation rules.

evidence.detail: R6 APD root defines error invariant apd-1.
R6 MedicinalProductDefinition has a route element with comments that it is the same concept as APD routeOfAdministration.code and they cannot be used together.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows the R6 pattern that violates apd-1 when the APD references a product that already has `route`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a cross-resource invariant that migration code must respect. Because R4 MPP required a route and R6 MedicinalProductDefinition can also carry route, a naive graph migration can duplicate route on both resources and become invalid.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: The break is potential rather than universal: it occurs only when `formOf` is populated and the referenced product has route. It is an error-level invariant, so conformant R6 validators should reject the graph.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Choose one route location. If using APD `routeOfAdministration`, leave `MedicinalProductDefinition.route` empty for referenced products; if route is maintained at product level, avoid creating APD instances that violate APD's mandatory route model or follow official guidance if available. Add integration tests that validate the whole resource graph, not only each resource in isolation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The invariant prevents inconsistent route duplication but makes migration order and graph context important. A warning-level constraint would have been easier for migration but weaker for conformance.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because APD `routeOfAdministration` is mandatory, the coexistence rule with MPD.route deserves human review for any migration design that also creates MedicinalProductDefinition resources.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds error invariant `apd-1`, requiring a referenced `formOf` MedicinalProductDefinition not to carry `route` when APD uses route-of-administration. This can invalidate migrated product graphs that duplicate route on both resources. The break is contextual rather than universal because R4 MPP has no `formOf` link, but graph migrations must choose one authoritative route location. The constraint appears proportionate because silently allowing duplicate route channels creates ambiguity for validators and consumers.
keyEvidence: R6 AdministrableProductDefinition root constraint apd-1 is severity error with expression `AdministrableProductDefinition.formOf.resolve().route.empty()`.
R6 AdministrableProductDefinition.routeOfAdministration is 1..* and its definition notes it cannot be used when the formOf product already uses route.
R6 MedicinalProductDefinition.route definition says it is the same concept as APD routeOfAdministration.code and they cannot be used together.
R4 MedicinalProductPharmaceutical has no formOf link, so the issue arises during broader R6 graph construction rather than direct field copying.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens the stability concern, and the break only appears in certain graph migrations. Regulatory route information is important enough that the error-level consistency rule still warrants treating it as real migration work.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid potential: a migrated R6 graph with APD.formOf resolving to an MPD that also has route fails an R6 error invariant, even if each individual route value is clinically equivalent.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-level invariant or an equivalence-based exception would be less disruptive. Those alternatives would preserve more transitional graphs but would weaken the duplicate-route rule and require difficult CodeableConcept equivalence or precedence logic when routes differ.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment: this is a contextual but legitimate R6 validation break with reasonable design tradeoffs.

findings.title: Route dosing definitions are generalized from clinical trial protocol context

oldState.summary: R4 dosing fields emphasize clinical trial authorization/protocol and investigational medicinal product context.

semanticText.definition: R4 definitions refer to first dose in humans, clinical trial protocols, maximum dose per day as per clinical trial authorization, and investigational medicinal product treatment period.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 text frames these route dosing elements around clinical trial or investigational product administration.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same cardinalities and datatypes but uses more general product-administration definitions.

semanticText.definition: R6 definitions refer generally to first dose, maximum single dose, maximum dose per day, maximum dose per treatment period, and maximum treatment period for the product.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 broadens the language from clinical trial/protocol-specific wording to general product administration.

facts.oldValue: The first dose administered in humans can be specified for a product under investigation.
facts.newValue: The first dose administered can be specified for the product.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same child paths and datatypes exist under the R6 routeOfAdministration tree.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a schema validation break because cardinalities and datatypes remain the same. It is a semantic/conformance risk for systems that interpreted the R4 fields as trial/protocol-specific rather than general product limits.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dose limit interpretation can be clinically relevant, even when the wire format is unchanged.

justification.inferredGoal: Broaden route dosing elements beyond investigational/clinical trial use.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable for R4-to-R6 instance compatibility; the dosing paths, types, and cardinalities are unchanged and the wording is broadened.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Broadening the dose-limit wording beyond investigational protocol context is plausible for an administrable product definition. The change can affect business assumptions for systems that treated these fields as trial-only, but it does not create a structural R4-to-R6 validation break. Under the calibration rubric, the backward-compatible-alternative question is therefore not applicable even though the semantic shift deserves migration attention.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Since no R4 instance becomes invalid because of this wording change, no less-breaking base design is needed for R4-to-R6 instance compatibility. R6 could have retained trial-specific wording and added separate general-dose fields or qualifiers, but that would be a semantic-clarity design alternative with duplicated dose concepts, not a backward-compatible rescue for invalid old data.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Separate trial-specific and general dosing fields could improve semantic clarity, but would duplicate dose-limit concepts rather than rescue invalid R4 instances.

evidence.detail: R4 definitions reference clinical trials, protocol, authorization, or investigational medicinal product context.
R6 definitions use general product administration wording with the same datatypes and cardinalities.

examples.examplesMd: No JSON example is needed; the risk is interpretation of unchanged fields rather than a changed JSON shape.

findings.narrativeMd: The route dosing fields are structurally stable but semantically broader in R6. Systems that treated R4 `maxDosePerDay` or `maxTreatmentPeriod` as specifically tied to clinical trial protocols may need to revisit rules and labels in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: FHIR validation is not expected to reject old values based on this text change. The compatibility risk is behavioral: business rules, UI labels, and analytics may interpret the same data as a general product limit rather than a trial-specific limit.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review business rules and user-facing labels for these dose limit fields. If a source value is specifically trial/protocol-derived, consider preserving that provenance in related authorization/trial resources or extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is a semantic broadening rather than a hard break. More explicit provenance or separate trial-specific fields would have reduced ambiguity but at a modeling cost.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The route dosing children keep their cardinalities and datatypes, while the definitions move from clinical-trial/protocol wording to more general product-administration wording. That can affect labels, documentation, or business interpretation, but it is not a structural validation break and does not require a different R6 base design to preserve old instances.
keyEvidence: R4 firstDose, maxSingleDose, maxDosePerDay, maxDosePerTreatmentPeriod, and maxTreatmentPeriod definitions mention clinical trial, protocol, authorization, or investigational product context.
R6 APD keeps the same child paths, max cardinalities, and Quantity/Ratio/Duration datatypes.
R6 definitions use more general product-administration wording.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use further lowers the concern because this is a prose broadening on unchanged optional fields, not a compatibility break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: business rules may need review if they assumed these fields were trial-only, but base validators and generated models see the same element shapes.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base design is needed for instance compatibility. Separate trial-specific and general dosing fields could improve semantic precision, but would duplicate dose-limit concepts rather than rescue invalid R4 data.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Low impact and Not applicable alternative judgment: this is migration-awareness text, not a material break.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: `identifier` remains `0..* Identifier` on the likely successor, with the same broad purpose of identifying the product.
`unitOfPresentation` remains `0..1 CodeableConcept`; R6 adds an example binding and clearer text, but no required validation constraint.

The main `routeOfAdministration` tree retains `1..* BackboneElement`, `code 1..1 CodeableConcept`, `firstDose/maxSingleDose/maxDosePerDay Quantity`, `maxDosePerTreatmentPeriod Ratio`, and `maxTreatmentPeriod Duration` in the APD successor. Semantic and cross-resource route issues are reported separately.

The veterinary `targetSpecies.withdrawalPeriod` subtree is preserved in the APD successor with the same required `tissue 1..1 CodeableConcept`, `value 1..1 Quantity`, and optional `supportingInformation 0..1 string`.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were found on the R4 resource or the matched APD successor elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limits were found on matched local elements.
No local slicing changes were found for the assigned R4 resource or the matched APD local element tree.

R4 local coded elements were largely unbound. R6 adds many example-strength bindings, which are not material validation breaks. Required publication-status bindings on APD `status` and `property.status` are covered in findings; SNOMED CT example ValueSets were not expanded.
No matched R4 local element other than inherited modifierExtension changed modifier semantics. The new APD `status` modifier is handled as a finding. Inherited base modifier behavior is out of scope.

Most matched local APD elements remain summary elements. New APD `description` is not summary and is optional; no standalone breaking summary-flag change was found beyond already reported successor additions.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 successor adds example bindings for many coded product fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Example-strength bindings on APD dose form, unit of presentation, route, target species, animal tissue type, property type, and ingredient do not by themselves make non-member codes invalid.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Even though these are not hard validation breaks, implementers should consider using the R6 example ValueSets for better interoperability and terminology QA.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Core route-of-administration subtree is substantially preserved in the likely successor
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Within the APD successor, the main route, dose-limit, target-species, and withdrawal-period child cardinalities and datatypes remain aligned with R4. The material route risks are the new cross-resource invariant and semantic wording changes, which are reported separately.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: This makes route details one of the more straightforward parts of the migration if the resource graph avoids duplicating route on `MedicinalProductDefinition.route`.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: This is the closest R6 successor and should own APD-local issues not specifically inherited from the R4 MPP comparison.
Detailed ingredient migration depends on a separate comparison of R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` to R6 `Ingredient`.
R6 `producedFrom` and manufactured dose form context may be needed for lossless migration from the R4 pharmaceutical product graph.
The APD `formOf` relationship and route duplication constraint depend on the R6 parent medicinal product model.
Co-packaged devices and contained items may need to migrate outside APD.device into package structures.
Publication-status is required for APD status and APD property status; local status vocabularies may need mapping.
Any inherited base-resource changes are intentionally out of scope for this local artifact report and should be handled by the base artifact analysis.
